budget_ms._comment: Budget for gate path [sys.executable, script] — no shell, real Python. During active OneDrive sync + Defender scanning, startup alone consumes 1700ms+. Values are p90 syncing-state gate-path totals observed 2026-09-23. Production path (shell=True) runs 1.8x slower — see FACTS.md §11.

_comment_interpreter_floor: Measured 2026-09-23 on Windows 11 / OneDrive (<org>) / Python 3.14.3. Method: subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass']). States: (1) quiet/idle: p50=534ms. (2) active OneDrive sync: p50=1707ms. (3) OneDrive paused (sync paused from tray): p50=1333ms — filter driver overhead persists even when sync is paused, because the driver intercepts file reads regardless of sync state. Running hook scripts from OneDrive costs ~5s additional when Defender scans the script file on first read — 6580ms gate-path vs 1333ms floor. Defender path exclusions (hooks-dir + Lib) reduce this to 1132ms during active sync (-37%). See FACTS.md §11.
_comment_kill_switch_headroom: Added to interpreter_floor_ms to get kill_threshold. 800ms covers stdlib imports (json/os/sys) plus Defender scan headroom. Total: floor(1700) + headroom(800) = 2500ms.
_comment_daemon_trigger: Two independent trigger paths for the Phase 4 daemon: (1) data-loss trigger from hook_log drop rate — daemon is justified if Stop hooks are being killed often enough to lose real memories; (2) latency trigger from doctor's live spawn measurement — daemon is justified if every turn has a noticeable pause even though no data is being lost. Both are needed: drop rate alone reads 0% while the tool is annoying enough to stop using.

daemon_trigger._comment_stop_drop_warn: Stop/UPS ratio below 98% over 50+ events → warn. 1 in 50 turns losing a candidate is the pain threshold. Set 2026-09-23 before real data; revisit after a week of sessions.
daemon_trigger._comment_stop_drop_daemon: Stop/UPS ratio below 95% → recommend daemon. 1 in 20 turns losing a candidate is unacceptable for a memory tool.
daemon_trigger._comment_min_events: Minimum hook_log entries before drop-rate recommendations fire. A week of real sessions.
daemon_trigger._section_latency: --- latency trigger (from doctor live spawn measurement) ---
daemon_trigger._comment_spawn_warn: Doctor measures interpreter spawn floor (python -c pass, x5, p50). Above 2000ms → warn. Rationale: post-exclusion target is ~1500ms; 2000ms means exclusions haven't been applied or aren't working. The 10s Stop timeout prevents data loss but does NOT make 2-5s pauses acceptable. Set against the POST-FIX target state, not the broken 5154ms state.
daemon_trigger._comment_spawn_daemon: Spawn floor p50 persistently above 3500ms → recommend daemon. Rationale: 3500ms per turn × 10 turns = 35s added latency per session. At that rate the tool's cost exceeds its value for most sessions. This threshold will be tripped in the broken state (5154ms) but should fall BELOW after exclusions land (~estimated 3000-3200ms, pending measurement). If post-exclusion spawn is still >3500ms, the daemon is the only remaining lever. Set 2026-09-23; mark as provisional until first post-exclusion measurement replaces the ⚠️ estimate in FACTS.md.
daemon_trigger._comment_duration_warn: hook_log.duration_ms p50 above this → DB or retrieval is unusually slow (separate from spawn). Normal within-Python work is ~55ms; 200ms suggests a DB issue.
